clue.text: Restive Hoskins is one getting nurses' attention

parts.note: Hoskins is the setter, so the setter saying 'Hoskins is' is I'M
a patient is someone nurses look after

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to fidgeting while being cared for in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym, so 'Hoskins is' becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restive is restless and unable to wait calmly, which is being impatient.

clue.text: I'm often unable to get off between the sheets

definitions.text: I'm often unable to get off between the sheets

parts.words: I'm often unable to get off between the sheets
parts.note: sounds like a sexual confession, but 'get off' means drop off to sleep

explanation.walkthrough: The innuendo of 'get off' in bed points to sex; the speaker simply cannot fall asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with chronic sleeplessness habitually lies awake in bed unable to doze.

clue.text: Climax with unknown character is seedy

parts.note: the peak is the climax or high point
Y is one of the algebraic symbols for an unknown

explanation.surface: A dodgy finale involving a mysterious figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaky is British slang for looking pale and unwell, which is what seedy can mean.

clue.text: US tabloid once

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 'us' as a collective, everyone
second meaning: a British Sunday tabloid, now the Sunday People

explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised 'US' looks like America; read as the pronoun 'us' it is all of us.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the general public, and was the title of a popular British Sunday paper.

clue.text: Downhearted, having lost head and kicked out

indicators.note: having lost its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: dejected means downhearted

explanation.surface: Someone thrown out is upset and has lost their cool.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ejected is to be thrown out or expelled, the same as kicked out.

clue.text: Row about a pair of model-types being more tawdry

indicators.note: about means the row goes around the other letters

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
the Model T was a Ford car, so two model-types is TT

explanation.surface: A quarrel over two fashion models looking increasingly cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model-types' suggests catwalk models, but it is the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby and cheap-looking, so its comparative means more tawdry.

clue.text: Outside appearance involving king is total shambles

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the appearance surrounds the king

parts.note: the face is the outward appearance of something, as in 'on the face of it'
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A royal occasion where the outward show is a complete mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A farce is a ridiculous, chaotic event, so a total shambles is an apt synonym.

clue.text: One well-upholstered sofa ripped around end of armrest

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters wrap the armrest's end
ripped suggests torn apart, so the letters are rearranged
end of means the last letter of armrest

parts.note: its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A torn sofa, well padded, with damage round the armrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-upholstered' looks like furniture talk but describes a plump person; the scrambled SOFA is FASO, split around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatso is a rude name for a fat person, someone jokingly said to be well-padded.

clue.text: Loser messing around with vote is former president

indicators.note: messing around means the letters are disordered together

explanation.surface: An election loser tampering with the ballot like a former leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt were both presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Characterful spirit English drunk served up around hotel

indicators.note: around means the reversed drunk encloses the hotel letter
in a down clue, served up means written upwards, reversing the drunk

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An English drunkard served drinks around a hotel bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests alcohol amid all the drinking, but it is the spirit of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the distinctive character or guiding spirit of a community or era.

clue.text: Report soldiers in mess close to revolt

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the mess plus its final letter

parts.note: a state is a mess, as in 'what a state your room is in'

indicators.note: close to means the end of the following word, revolt

parts.note: its final letter is used
men is a common term for soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: A news report about troops in the canteen nearly rising up.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldiers sit inside STATE plus T, the close of 'revolt', splitting it as STATE-MEN-T.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a formal account or declaration, a synonym for a report.

clue.text: Short blast then bit of honk … canine?

parts.note: a toot is a short blast on a horn

indicators.note: a bit of the word honk here means only its first letter

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A dog's bark is likened to a car horn's quick toot and honk.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'canine' sound like a dog; it is the pointed tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A canine is one of the pointed teeth beside the incisors, so it is a kind of tooth.

clue.text: Former PM and bishop getting MDMA, perhaps

parts.note: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister
B is the chess notation for bishop
MDMA is the drug ecstasy, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A tabloid scandal: an ex-premier and a clergyman caught with party drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe and perhaps are both adverbs expressing possibility, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Comic also tries to get lady in stitches

indicators.note: comic means farcical or absurd, so the letters are played around with

explanation.surface: A comedian works hard to make a woman laugh uncontrollably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In stitches' suggests helpless laughter, but here it means sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailoress is a woman who makes clothes, working with needle and stitches.

clue.text: Hot drink yours truly had lacking flavour

parts.note: hot can mean fashionable, which is in
to sip is to drink
yours truly is I, and 'I had' contracts to I'D

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the hot drink they had was bland.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food or drink is tasteless and weak, so it lacks flavour.

clue.text: Drink at end of day with star on barbiturate?

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: the sun is a star
a downer is a depressant drug such as a barbiturate

explanation.surface: A celebrity mixing evening drinks with sleeping pills.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset, a British colonial custom.

clue.text: Breed with nurse with ultimately toned bum

parts.note: to rear animals is to breed them
EN stands for enrolled nurse

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the closing letter of toned

parts.note: its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A fitness tale of a nurse who works out to firm up her behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Rear end is a colloquial term for the buttocks, which is what bum means in British slang.

clue.text: Drug a nice gal's sorted

indicators.note: sorted means put into a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nice girl's drugs are sorted out, as if supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic is a painkilling medicine, a kind of drug.

clue.text: Forged deeds Tory put through the shredder?

indicators.note: forged means fabricated, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Fake property papers belonging to a Conservative get shredded.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that shredding is only one way of being destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredding papers destroys them, so this is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Tory offensive about northern 'insiders'

definitions.note: plural in the clue, but content as a mass noun covers everything inside

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the offensive wraps around northern

parts.note: the Tet offensive was a 1968 campaign in the Vietnam War

explanation.surface: A Conservative attack on people from the north who are in the know.
explanation.definitionFit: Content is what is held within something, so the quotation-marked 'insiders' playfully describes it.

clue.text: Tall leader longs for short folk

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Tall

parts.note: its first letter is used
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A tall man in charge yearns for small people, a comic contrast.
explanation.walkthrough: Titch is British slang for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Titches is informal British slang for small people, so short folk.

clue.text: Those under fire hit at front in Scottish squad

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the team's name

parts.note: Hearts (Heart of Midlothian) is an Edinburgh football club

indicators.note: at front means just the opening letter of hit

parts.note: its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A Scottish team takes heavy hits and finds itself under attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under fire' sounds like being attacked; a hearth literally sits beneath the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearth is the floor of a fireplace, placed literally beneath the burning fire.

clue.text: Woman likely to have the most lines of smack, I'm told

definitions.text: Woman likely to have the most lines

indicators.note: I'm told means as heard, so the drug's name is spoken aloud

parts.note: smack is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Lines of a powdered drug, a joke about who has the most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' and 'smack' point to drug-taking, but the lines are a script's dialogue.
explanation.definitionFit: The female lead in a film or play usually has the largest speaking part.

clue.text: The Lord will save old Queen singer

indicators.note: saving something means keeping it safe within, so old goes inside

parts.note: Christ is called the Lord
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A hymn-like hope that the Lord will rescue the elderly monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a choir, especially a church choir, so a singer.

clue.text: I make love with one in a quiver!

definitions.text: I make love with one in a quiver!

parts.words: I make love with one in a quiver!
parts.note: sounds racy, but the god of love makes people fall in love with an arrow from his quiver

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiver' suggests trembling passion; it is the case holding the archer god's arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love fires arrows that cause people to fall in love.

clue.text: Not all abide asinine thoughts

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not everyone tolerates foolish opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are notions formed in the mind, so they are thoughts.

clue.text: Tiger Woods is one to sack large caddy, perhaps

indicators.note: to sack is to dismiss, so large is thrown out of the word

parts.note: Tiger Woods is a famous golfer
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Tiger Woods is about to fire a big caddie.
explanation.definitionFit: A gofer runs errands for someone, and a caddie fetching and carrying is an example.

clue.text: Those heading for airboat relay some impolite language

indicators.note: those heading means the letters at the head of each following word

explanation.surface: Travellers on a swamp boat pass on some rude words.
explanation.definitionFit: Farsi, or Persian, is the main language of Iran.

clue.text: Criminal making fellow pressure coppers

indicators.note: making fellow pressure means turning the F into P

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who handles stolen goods
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A crook leans on a colleague in order to pressure the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police officers, but it means copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennies are copper-coloured coins, so 'coppers' is slang for small change in pence.

clue.text: Setter in do Harry gets drunk with a sip

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: At a party Harry takes a sip and gets tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' seems to be the crossword compiler and 'do' a party; read as a 'hairdo', the setter is what holds it in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairspray is applied to set a hairstyle, or hairdo, so it is a setter in a do.

clue.text: Game trollops taking top off for daughter

indicators.note: the opening letter is removed and daughter put in its place

parts.note: tart and trollop are both old insults for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: Floozies stripping off for a man's daughter in some saucy contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a pub sport of throwing small arrows at a board.

clue.text: Relation huffs about possible Congressional result

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the sulks are read backwards

parts.note: pets are fits of sulking, as in 'in a pet'
a child can result from congress, a dated word for sex

explanation.surface: A relative grumbles about what might come out of the US Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congressional' seems to be the American legislature but means sexual congress.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepchild is a spouse's child from another partner, a family relation by marriage.
